summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE, and chronic pelvic fractures was admitted for acute abdominal pain, fever, nausea, and vomiting. Initial evaluation revealed tachycardia, leukopenia, and elevated lactate of 7.2, concerning for sepsis. CT imaging showed procto-sigmoid colitis, prompting treatment with intravenous ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, later transitioned to oral therapy. Stool studies were negative for C. difficile, Salmonella, and Shigella. Her nausea did not improve with ondansetron, so metoclopramide (Reglan) was started with good effect. Lactate normalized, symptoms improved, and she resumed a regular diet. Her cirrhosis remained stable, with no encephalopathy or ascites progression. The spironolactone was held during vomiting and restarted at discharge. A small liver lesion suggestive of HCC recurrence was noted, with plans for RFA. She completed antibiotic therapy, was discharged home, and advised to follow up with liver, GI, and primary care teams.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver with ascites
